Discover, inquire and tryStarter2–3 weeks

Coaching inquiry and discovery call funnel

Turn Instagram comments and DMs, ad leads and WhatsApp messages into booked discovery calls with a short pre-call form, so coaches speak to prepared prospects and nobody waits days for a reply.

Nutrition & online coaching

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Online coaches get most inquiries through Instagram reels, DMs and WhatsApp, often late at night. Replies depend on the coach's free time, prospects ask the same questions about price and approach, and serious people wait days for a call. Mass DM tools that message people who never wrote in, or that promise results, damage trust and break platform rules.

Trigger

A comment keyword or DM on the coach's Instagram professional account, a Meta lead form, a website inquiry or a message to the WhatsApp Business number.

How it runs

  1. Reply only to the person who wrote in, inside the platform's messaging window. AI matches the question to an approved answer on approach, format and published prices; anything else goes to the coach.
  2. Ask a few qualifying questions: goal, timeline, preferred language and a yes or no on whether they are being treated for a medical condition.
  3. Offer discovery call slots from the coach's calendar and send a short pre-call form that states the call is not medical advice.
  4. Route prospects who mention a medical condition, pregnancy or a history of disordered eating to the qualified dietitian rather than a sales coach.
  5. Send an approved reminder before the call and, to people who opted in, a recap with program options and a payment link after it.
  6. Log source, stage and outcome in the CRM so content and ad spend are compared by enrollments, not likes.

Human checkpoint

The coach or dietitian runs every discovery call and decides whether the program suits the person. Anyone who mentions a medical condition is routed to a qualified professional. Automated replies never promise results, diagnose or suggest diets.

Discover, inquire and tryStandard3–5 weeks

Trial class booking and membership conversion

Book trial classes and intro offers straight from ads, Google and WhatsApp, prepare the trainer or teacher, and follow up after the visit with published plans and a payment link, so every trial visitor gets a consistent path to membership.

Gyms & fitness studios · Yoga & wellness centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Gyms and studios pay for ads and give away trial passes, but trial visitors often arrive unannounced, train with whoever is free and leave without a conversation. Follow-up depends on which consultant is on shift, no-shows are never offered another slot, and nobody can say which campaign produced members rather than one-off visits.

Trigger

A Click-to-WhatsApp ad, Meta lead form, Google Business Profile message, website form or front-desk walk-in entry asking for a trial class or intro offer.

How it runs

  1. Capture the lead with source, goal, preferred time and messaging consent, and check for an existing member or lead record.
  2. Offer trial slots from the live class or floor schedule and confirm with an approved WhatsApp template covering what to bring and where to enter.
  3. Send a pre-exercise readiness questionnaire such as PAR-Q+ through a secure link; any yes answer is shown to the trainer, who asks for the person's doctor's clearance where needed.
  4. Brief the assigned trainer or teacher the evening before with goal, experience and questionnaire flags.
  5. Mark attendance from the check-in system, then give the consultant a follow-up task with the trainer's note and approved plan options.
  6. Send the visitor a recap with published plans and a payment link; no-shows get one approved offer to rebook.
  7. Report inquiries, trials booked, trials attended and memberships by campaign and consultant.

Human checkpoint

The trainer reviews readiness answers before the session and decides whether medical clearance is needed. The membership consultant owns the conversation, pricing and any discount within the limits the owner sets. Automation never diagnoses or tells anyone they are fit to exercise.

Join, pay and onboardStandard4–6 weeks

Coaching intake and qualified plan workflow

Collect consented intake details through a secure form, route them to a qualified dietitian or nutritionist, and let AI handle the formatting work around the plan the professional writes, such as shopping lists and recipe swaps.

Nutrition & online coaching

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Coaching businesses grow faster than their qualified staff. Intake details arrive through chats and documents, sales coaches are sometimes asked to write plans they are not qualified to write, and clients with diabetes, thyroid conditions, pregnancy or a history of disordered eating can end up on generic templates. Professionals lose hours to formatting instead of judgment.

Trigger

A client completes enrollment and payment for a coaching program.

How it runs

  1. Send a secure intake form on the business's own domain with a clear notice of what is collected, why, who sees it and for how long, plus separate consent for optional items such as progress photos.
  2. Collect goals, routine, food preferences and allergies, medical conditions, current medicines and recent lab reports if the client chooses to share them.
  3. Check the intake against referral rules agreed with the lead dietitian; listed conditions route the client to their doctor or a clinical dietitian before any plan.
  4. Assign the client to a qualified professional by caseload, language and specialty, with a due date for the first plan.
  5. The professional writes the plan in the coaching platform; AI then drafts shopping lists, regional or vegetarian swaps and a plain-language summary for the professional to approve.
  6. Deliver the approved plan through the client portal and schedule the first weekly check-in.

Human checkpoint

A qualified dietitian or nutritionist writes and signs off every plan and every change to it. Clients who report a condition on the referral list see their doctor or a clinical dietitian first. AI never sets calorie targets, recommends supplements or gives medical advice.

Join, pay and onboardStandard3–5 weeks

Retreat, workshop and teacher training enrollment

Run applications, deposits, installments, health declarations, room allocation and pre-arrival information for retreats, workshops and teacher trainings from one record, with the lead teacher deciding every application that needs judgment.

Yoga & wellness centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Retreats and teacher trainings are high-value programs with many moving parts: applications, eligibility, deposits, installment plans, room sharing, dietary needs, travel details and waitlists. They are usually run across spreadsheets, WhatsApp groups and bank statements, so payments are missed, places are double-sold and health information sits in chats.

Trigger

A new application on the program page, or a waitlisted applicant when a place opens.

How it runs

  1. Collect the application through a secure form with experience level, emergency contact, dietary needs and a short health declaration with explicit consent.
  2. Route applications with health flags or eligibility questions to the lead teacher, who accepts, asks for more information or declines.
  3. Send accepted applicants a deposit link and an installment schedule that matches the published cancellation and refund terms.
  4. Remind applicants before each installment, and alert the program manager when a payment is overdue instead of releasing a place automatically.
  5. Allocate rooms by sharing preference, and fill released places from the waitlist in order.
  6. Send the approved pre-arrival pack with schedule, packing list and directions, and give the teaching team a health and dietary summary limited to what they need.

Human checkpoint

The lead teacher decides every application with health flags or eligibility questions. The program manager approves exceptions to payment schedules, transfers and refunds. Health declarations are read by people and never scored automatically.

Book, attend and visitStandard3–4 weeks

Class booking, waitlists and automatic promotion

Let members book classes on WhatsApp or the app, hold fair waitlists, offer the next person a spot when one opens, and apply the late cancellation policy the same way every time.

Gyms & fitness studios · Yoga & wellness centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Early-morning, evening and weekend classes fill in minutes, while members who book and do not show block others. Waitlists live on paper or in personal chats, front desks apply late cancellation rules differently, and instructors walk in without knowing who is new or returning from an injury.

Trigger

A member books, cancels or joins a waitlist in the app, on the website or by WhatsApp, or a class reaches its cancellation cutoff.

How it runs

  1. Read the timetable, capacity, spots held for aggregator bookings and member entitlements through the studio software's API or scheduled exports, and accept WhatsApp bookings from members who opted in.
  2. Place members on an ordered waitlist when a class is full, and tell them their position.
  3. When a spot opens before the cutoff, offer it to the next person with a short window to accept, then move down the list.
  4. Send a reminder before class with an easy cancel link, and the joining link for online classes, then release unconfirmed spots at the agreed time.
  5. Apply the published late cancellation rule, such as a forfeited class credit, and queue repeat no-shows and any fee for the manager instead of charging automatically.
  6. Give the instructor a class list that marks first-timers and members who noted an injury, without the details.

Human checkpoint

The studio manager sets capacity, cutoffs and the late cancellation policy, and personally decides any fee, credit deduction or booking restriction for repeat no-shows. Instructors decide how to adapt a class for anyone flagged.

Book, attend and visitStandard3–5 weeks

Salon booking, reminders and no-show handling

Book the right service with the right stylist or therapist for the right length of time, send reminders and patch test prompts, fill late gaps from a waitlist, and handle no-shows with one clear policy.

Salons & spas

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Salons take bookings by phone, Instagram, WhatsApp and walk-in. Service length varies by stylist and hair length, color needs processing time, spa treatments need a room and a trained therapist, and color clients may need an allergy alert (patch) test first. No-shows on long services leave expensive gaps, and deposit rules change with each receptionist.

Trigger

A booking request on WhatsApp, Instagram or the website, a change in the appointment book, or an appointment reaching a reminder or no-show checkpoint.

How it runs

  1. AI maps free-text requests on WhatsApp or Instagram to a service, and unclear ones go to reception. The booking is matched to stylists or therapists trained for it, using durations, processing time and rooms.
  2. Offer real open slots, confirm with an approved template, and send a deposit link for long or high-value services where the salon's policy asks for one.
  3. For color services, check the client card for a recent patch test and prompt the client to book one ahead of the visit where the product instructions require it.
  4. Send reminders before the appointment with easy reschedule and cancel options.
  5. Offer late cancellations to clients waitlisted for that service and stylist.
  6. Mark no-shows, send a polite message with the policy, and queue deposit or fee decisions for the manager.

Human checkpoint

The salon manager approves every deposit retention, fee and booking restriction. Stylists check patch test results in person and decide whether a service goes ahead. Anyone reporting a reaction is told to stop and seek medical advice, and the manager is alerted.

Book, attend and visitStarter2–4 weeks

Stylist and therapist commission and incentive statements

Calculate commissions and incentives on services, packages and retail from the salon's own billing records, show each stylist or therapist a running statement, and give the owner a reviewed payout sheet at month end.

Salons & spas

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Salon pay usually mixes a fixed salary with commission on services, different rates for color, chemical and spa work, package redemptions, retail sales and targets. When the calculation lives in spreadsheets, staff cannot see where they stand, discounts and redos are treated inconsistently, and month end becomes a dispute.

Trigger

Each completed and billed service or retail sale, plus the month-end close.

How it runs

  1. Pull completed services, package redemptions, retail lines, discounts and refunds from the salon software and POS every night.
  2. Apply the written commission plan: rates by service category, treatment of discounts, redos and package value, and targets or slabs.
  3. Use service values net of GST, so commission is calculated on the salon's revenue rather than on tax collected.
  4. Give each stylist or therapist a private running statement with the line items behind it.
  5. Let staff raise a query on any line, which goes to the manager with the bill attached.
  6. At month end, produce a payout sheet for owner approval and export it to payroll or accounting.

Human checkpoint

The owner or HR lead approves the commission plan, every manual adjustment and the final payout sheet. The manager resolves queries against the original bill. The automation calculates; it never changes pay rules or pays anyone on its own.

Train, track and engageStandard3–5 weeks

Attendance-drop alerts and trainer check-ins

Spot members and students whose visits fall below their own usual pattern, brief their trainer or teacher with context and a drafted personal message, and track whether anyone followed up, well before the renewal date.

Gyms & fitness studios · Yoga & wellness centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Members rarely cancel on the day they lose motivation. They come less, then stop, then let the plan lapse. Access logs and class bookings show this weeks in advance, but nobody looks at them, and generic win-back offers sent after expiry arrive too late and feel impersonal.

Trigger

A nightly job over access control check-ins, class bookings and plan dates.

How it runs

  1. Build each member's usual pattern from recent check-ins and bookings, excluding approved freezes, travel and new joiners still settling in.
  2. Flag members whose visits fall clearly below their own pattern, using simple rules the owner can read, such as no visit in twice their usual gap.
  3. Add context for the trainer: usual time, last class, PT package status, renewal date and the latest note on the member's record.
  4. Draft a short personal note for the trainer to edit, such as a class suggestion, never a discount by default. Outside WhatsApp's 24-hour window an approved template opens the conversation, and the note follows when the member replies.
  5. Send health-related replies, such as injury, illness or pregnancy, to a person, with a suggestion to consult a doctor before the program changes.
  6. Track whether each flag was worked, what the member said and whether they returned.

Human checkpoint

Trainers or teachers decide whether and how to reach out, and edit every drafted message before it is sent. Any offer or discount needs the manager's approval. Health-related replies go to a person and are never answered by automation.

Train, track and engageStarter2–4 weeks

Personal training package and session tracking

Track every PT package from sale to last session: sessions booked, completed and remaining, expiry reminders, trainer session logs and a monthly trainer statement that matches each member's balance.

Gyms & fitness studios

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Personal training is sold as packages of sessions with an expiry date, then tracked on paper cards or trainers' phones. Members lose track of their balance, sessions expire unused and turn into disputes, trainers argue over counts at payout time, and owners cannot see which trainers keep their clients.

Trigger

A PT package sale, a booked or completed session, or a package nearing its expiry date or last session.

How it runs

  1. Create the package from the POS or gym software sale with sessions, price, trainer and expiry date.
  2. The trainer confirms each completed session in the staff app, and the member gets a short message with the remaining balance.
  3. Remind the member and trainer when sessions remain close to expiry, so they can be booked in time.
  4. Prompt the trainer when two sessions remain to discuss next steps with the member, without automatic upsell messages.
  5. Route extension and transfer requests to the manager under the written package policy.
  6. Produce a monthly trainer statement of completed sessions and incentives that reconciles with member balances.

Human checkpoint

Trainers confirm sessions and own the renewal conversation. The manager approves extensions, transfers, refunds and any dispute over session counts. Trainers write and adjust exercise programs; the automation only tracks and reminds.

Train, track and engageStandard3–5 weeks

Weekly coaching check-ins and progress logs

Send a structured weekly check-in, keep measurements, adherence notes and optional photos in one place, summarize each week for the coach, and send concerns to a qualified professional before anything else happens.

Nutrition & online coaching

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Coaches receive check-ins as long WhatsApp messages, voice notes, screenshots and photos at all hours. Reading and replying takes evenings, history is hard to see in one place, and the occasional warning sign, such as fainting, very rapid weight loss or signs of disordered eating, can be missed in the volume.

Trigger

The client's scheduled check-in day, or a check-in submitted early.

How it runs

  1. Send an approved reminder with a link to a short check-in form: weight or measurements if the client chooses, adherence, energy, sleep, hunger, questions and optional photos.
  2. Store the check-in against the client's history and chart the trends the coach needs at a glance.
  3. AI summarizes the week for the coach, quoting the client's own words and listing the questions to answer.
  4. Concern rules agreed with the lead dietitian, such as dizziness, rapid weight change or signs of disordered eating, send the check-in to a qualified professional at once and pause routine replies.
  5. The coach writes or edits the reply; plan changes are made only by the qualified professional who owns the plan.
  6. Flag clients who miss two check-ins to the coach for a personal message.

Human checkpoint

Coaches review every summary and send every reply themselves. Plan changes are made only by the qualified dietitian or nutritionist. Concern flags reach a qualified professional the same day, and clients with possible medical issues are advised to see their doctor.

Aftercare notes and consented product suggestions

Send each client the stylist's or therapist's own aftercare notes and the products they actually recommended at the visit, with consent, and track retail follow-through without generic promotional blasts.

Salons & spas

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Clients forget aftercare advice by the time they get home, and retail suggestions depend on who was on shift. Generic product blasts feel pushy, AI-generated skin or scalp diagnoses would overstep what a salon should claim, and product claims copied from brand material can break advertising rules.

Trigger

A service is closed in the salon software with aftercare notes or recommended products on the client card.

How it runs

  1. The stylist or therapist selects aftercare notes and a few recommended products on the service card before checkout.
  2. After the visit, send the aftercare notes, and add the product list only for clients who said yes to product suggestions.
  3. Use approved product descriptions only, without medical, cure or promised-result claims.
  4. Offer the products through the salon's own store link or for pickup at the next visit.
  5. Ask a short feedback question after an agreed period and route any reported irritation or reaction to the manager.
  6. Report retail attach rate and follow-through by stylist and service.

Human checkpoint

Stylists and therapists choose every recommendation themselves; AI only tidies the wording of their notes. Any client reporting irritation, a burn or a reaction is called by the manager and advised to seek medical advice.

Renew, rebook or pauseStandard3–5 weeks

Renewals, freezes and payment recovery

Tell members clearly before a plan ends or auto-renews, offer renew, change, freeze or cancel options under the written policy, recover failed payments politely, and keep one record of every decision.

Gyms & fitness studios · Yoga & wellness centres · Nutrition & online coaching

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Renewal reminders, freeze requests and failed payments are tracked in registers and personal chats. Some members are surprised by a debit, others cannot find how to cancel, freeze rules depend on who answers, and failed UPI Autopay or card debits are chased days late, if at all.

Trigger

A plan approaching its end or renewal date, a freeze or cancellation request, or a failed payment event from the gateway.

How it runs

  1. Before the end or renewal date, send an approved message with the plan, price, date and options to renew, change, freeze or cancel.
  2. Members who renew pay by link or set up UPI Autopay or a card mandate through the gateway; the bank's pre-debit notice and authentication stay with the gateway.
  3. Take freeze requests through a short form. Requests inside the written policy are applied where the software's API allows, or queued for the front desk; others go to the manager with the member's history.
  4. Make cancellation as easy as joining: a clear link or reply, a confirmation and the end date, with no repeated retention calls.
  5. When a debit fails, send a polite notice with a fresh payment link, retry only as the gateway and mandate rules allow, and alert the front desk after an agreed number of attempts.
  6. Members who let a plan lapse get one approved win-back message after an agreed gap, only if they gave marketing consent.

Human checkpoint

The manager approves freezes outside policy, refunds, transfers, pro-rata adjustments and any discount. Front-desk staff call members with repeated payment failures. Automation never blocks access or ends a plan without a person's decision, except to carry out a member's own cancellation.

Renew, rebook or pauseStarter2–3 weeks

Service-based rebooking reminders

Remind each client when their next service is due, based on the service they had and the interval their stylist recommends, with a one-tap link to book the same stylist.

Salons & spas

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Clients who leave without booking their next visit often drift, and a root touch-up, keratin refresh, beard trim, facial or nail infill each has its own natural interval. Front desks cannot track that for hundreds of clients, and generic monthly offers ignore when each person is actually due.

Trigger

A completed service in the salon software, plus a daily check for clients reaching their recommended interval without a future booking.

How it runs

  1. Set default rebooking intervals per service with the salon, which stylists can adjust on each client card.
  2. At checkout, prompt the receptionist to offer the next appointment before the client leaves.
  3. For clients without a future booking, send an approved reminder near the due date with the stylist's next open slots.
  4. If the usual stylist has left or is on leave, offer an equally trained colleague without explaining why.
  5. Stop after one follow-up, and move clients well past their interval to an occasional consented check-in.

Human checkpoint

Stylists set or change the interval for each client. The salon manager approves the default intervals and the reminder wording. Any offer or discount in a reminder needs manager approval.

Review, refer and returnStarter2–4 weeks

Feedback, review invitations and referral program

Ask every client for private feedback after a visit or milestone, invite everyone to review the same way, route problems to a manager, and run a referral program whose rewards are never tied to reviews.

Gyms & fitness studios · Salons & spas · Yoga & wellness centres · Nutrition & online coaching

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Google reviews drive local discovery for gyms, salons and studios, and referrals drive many coaching sign-ups. But review requests are ad hoc, staff are sometimes told to ask clients to name them or to hit a review count, and referral rewards are tracked by hand. Incentives and asking only happy clients break Google's review rules, and quotas push staff toward both.

Trigger

A completed visit, a milestone such as the first month of membership, the end of a PT package or program, or a client sharing a referral link.

How it runs

  1. Send a short private feedback form after the visit or milestone.
  2. Open a recovery task for the manager on low scores, with the visit details, so the client hears from a person.
  3. Send every client the same review invitation regardless of their score, with no incentive and no request to name staff.
  4. Draft replies to new public reviews with AI from approved facts, for the manager to edit and approve.
  5. Give each member a personal referral link; rewards apply only when the referred person joins, under published terms, and never depend on a review.
  6. Report feedback themes, review coverage and referral joins by location and team.

Human checkpoint

The manager handles every low score personally and approves every public reply, refund or goodwill gesture. Referral rewards beyond the published terms need owner approval. Staff are never given review quotas.
